newsitem.title: CANADA: S.Africa's Stals sees gradual fx controls removal.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Stals sees gradual fx controls removal.

text.p: Chris Stals, governor of the South Africa Reserve Bank, said on Friday that South Africa would only phase out its foreign exchange controls on a gradual basis.
"The remaining exchange controls will be phased out gradually," Stals said at the 39th annual congress of the Association Cambiste Internationale.

Stal's said the central bank's level of foreign reserve is still very low. He described the level of reserves, which are currently about $5.0 billion, as "more comfortable (than in the past) but still inadequate."
The governor said that government and reserve bank acknowledged that rapid elimination of currency controls could have an sharp impact on the country.

"The adjustments costs of an immediate abolition of foreign exchange controls would not be tolerable," Stals said, He said the risk was the economic impact would force the government to step into the conduct of exchange rate policy.

Stals said there was no predetermined level at which the reserve bank would like to see rand exchange rate, but he noted that moves of more than 20 percent over short periods of time were clearly of some concern.
Stals also said the country's elections in 1999 would not alter financial policy.

"As far as economic policies are concerned and the implementation of monetary policy I am almost sure as I stand here today that there will be no major changes in the South African situation after the next election," Stals said.

He also said he expected the African National Congress which captured some 65 percent of the vote in the previous elections, to return to power in 1999. The succesor to President Nelson Mandela will continue current economic policies, he said.
